payload.task_text:
I am writing a comparative analysis of chain-of-thought reasoning methods for my research group. Please look up the chain-of-thought reasoning papers in the arxiv-latex database and help me organize the findings. The database holds several papers, but only five are about chain-of-thought reasoning methods; the others are about word representations and are out of scope. The five reasoning papers, by arXiv ID, are: 2201.11903, 2203.11171, 2205.11916, 2210.03493, and 2305.10601. Use the arxiv-latex tools (get_paper_prompt or get_paper_abstract) with these IDs to retrieve each paper's title and abstract.

Create a Google Sheet called "Reasoning Methods Comparison" with a sheet named "Papers" that lists the reasoning-related papers. The columns should be Title, Year, Method, and Key_Contribution. For the Method column, try to identify the main reasoning approach described in each paper (for example "chain-of-thought prompting", "self-consistency", "zero-shot CoT", "automatic CoT", or "tree of thoughts"). For Key_Contribution, write a brief one-sentence description of the paper's main contribution. Only include papers that are about reasoning methods, not papers about word embeddings or word representations.

Also create a Word document called "Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx" in my workspace. The document should have the title "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison" at the top, followed by today's date (2026-03-06). Then include a section for each reasoning paper, mentioning its title and briefly describing its contribution. End with a short conclusion paragraph.

Note: this task has two deliverables — the Google Sheet and the Word document. If you are running as a team of agents, divide the work between agents (for example, assign the spreadsheet to one agent and the Word document to another) or otherwise serialize your writes, so that both deliverables are completed without conflicting writes to the same file.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent itself retrieves the five fixed papers' title and abstract (five light read-only calls, no research wave), freezes one canonical five-row packet, and dispatches exactly one parallel writer wave of two independent deliverable owners.

Before the wave, the main agent resolves the runtime workspace, freezes the five explicit arXiv IDs — 2201.11903, 2203.11171, 2205.11916, 2210.03493, 2305.10601 — and today's required displayed date 2026-03-06. It calls the arxiv-latex abstract/prompt retrieval once per ID, extracts title/year/method label/key contribution from the returned abstracts only, excludes all word-representation material, and freezes five literal rows {arxiv_id, title, year, method, key_contribution} plus per-ID retrieval controls.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel:

1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): The Google Sheet writer: create a spreadsheet titled exactly "Reasoning Methods Comparison" with exactly one sheet named "Papers" (rename the default sheet or create the named one), write the header row Title, Year, Method, Key_Contribution followed by exactly the five frozen rows, then read the complete range back and return the spreadsheet/sheet IDs, header check and row count. Do not create the Word document.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): The Word writer: create Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx in the resolved workspace with the title "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison", the literal date 2026-03-06, one section per frozen paper mentioning its title and contribution, and a short conclusion paragraph, then read the document outline and text back. Do not create the spreadsheet.

The two writers serialize only through their own distinct files and never touch each other's deliverable. After the wave, the main agent reconciles both read-backs against the frozen packet (five rows/sections each, exact title/date, reasoning-only scope) and calls claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent and do not add a verification wave.

nodes.text:
Create a Google Spreadsheet for a research group's comparative analysis of chain-of-thought reasoning papers.

Requirements:
1. Create a new Google Spreadsheet titled exactly "Reasoning Methods Comparison".
2. It must contain a sheet named exactly "Papers". If the new spreadsheet's default sheet has a different name (e.g., "Sheet1"), rename it to "Papers" (or create a "Papers" sheet and populate that).
3. In the "Papers" sheet, write a header row with these exact column names: Title, Year, Method, Key_Contribution
4. Then write exactly these 5 data rows (row order as listed):

Row 1: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models | 2022 | Chain-of-thought prompting | Shows that prompting large language models to generate a series of intermediate reasoning steps significantly improves performance on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning benchmarks.

Row 2: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models | 2022 | Self-consistency | Introduces a decoding strategy that samples a diverse set of reasoning paths and selects the most consistent answer by marginalizing out the sampled paths, replacing naive greedy decoding in chain-of-thought prompting.

Row 3: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners | 2022 | Zero-shot CoT | Demonstrates that simply adding "Let's think step by step" before each answer enables large language models to perform zero-shot chain-of-thought reasoning without any few-shot demonstrations.

Row 4: Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models | 2022 | Automatic CoT (Auto-CoT) | Proposes Auto-CoT, which automatically constructs demonstrations of questions and reasoning chains via clustering and zero-shot CoT generation, eliminating the need for manually crafted exemplars.

Row 5: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models | 2023 | Tree of thoughts | Introduces the Tree of Thoughts framework, which generalizes chain-of-thought prompting by enabling exploration over coherent units of text ("thoughts") in a tree structure for deliberate problem solving.

Only these 5 reasoning-method papers should appear — do not add any papers about word embeddings or word representations.

Deliverable/acceptance criteria: The spreadsheet exists with title "Reasoning Methods Comparison", contains a sheet named "Papers" with the header row and all 5 rows exactly as specified. Report back the spreadsheet ID and a confirmation of what was written.
Create reasoning comparison Google Sheet

Create a Word document named exactly "Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx" in the directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Kimi-K3/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-reasoning-gsheet/workspace (use that full path for the filename).

Document structure and content:
1. At the top, a title (Heading 1 style or equivalent): "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison"
2. On the next line, the date: 2026-03-06
3. Then a section for each of the following five papers (use a sub-heading, e.g., Heading 2, with the paper's title, followed by a short paragraph describing its contribution based on the provided abstract info):

Paper 1: "Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models" (2022)
Contribution: Explores how generating a chain of thought — a series of intermediate reasoning steps — significantly improves the ability of large language models to perform complex reasoning, showing gains on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning benchmarks. Method: chain-of-thought prompting.

Paper 2: "Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models" (2022)
Contribution: Introduces self-consistency, a decoding strategy that replaces naive greedy decoding in chain-of-thought prompting by sampling a diverse set of reasoning paths and then selecting the most consistent answer by marginalizing out the sampled reasoning paths. Method: self-consistency.

Paper 3: "Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners" (2022)
Contribution: Shows that simply adding "Let's think step by step" before each answer significantly enables zero-shot chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models, without requiring few-shot demonstrations. Method: zero-shot CoT.

Paper 4: "Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models" (2022)
Contribution: Proposes Auto-CoT, which automatically constructs demonstrations with questions and reasoning chains using clustering and zero-shot CoT generation, removing the need for hand-crafted demonstration examples. Method: automatic CoT (Auto-CoT).

Paper 5: "Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models" (2023)
Contribution: Introduces the Tree of Thoughts framework, which generalizes chain-of-thought prompting by enabling language models to explore coherent units of text ("thoughts") in a tree structure, supporting deliberate problem solving beyond left-to-right token-level decisions. Method: tree of thoughts.

4. End with a short conclusion paragraph (3-5 sentences) summarizing the progression of chain-of-thought reasoning methods: from few-shot CoT prompting, through improved decoding (self-consistency), zero-shot elicitation, automatic demonstration construction, to tree-structured exploration (Tree of Thoughts) — noting that these methods collectively broaden LLM reasoning capabilities.

Include only these five reasoning-method papers — nothing about word embeddings or word representations.

Deliverable/acceptance criteria: The file /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Kimi-K3/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-reasoning-gsheet/workspace/Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx exists and contains the title, the date 2026-03-06, one section per paper (5 sections) with its title and contribution description, and a conclusion paragraph. Report back the file path and a brief outline of what was written.
